According to the javadoc, `subList` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException` if `fromIndex < 0 || toIndex > size || fromIndex > toIndex`. Both calls use `fromIndex = 1` and `toIndex = components.size()`. Before the first call, there are checks: `if (components.size() == 0)` throws an exception, ensuring size > 0. Then `if (requireProto && Helper.isNullOrEmpty(components.get(0)))` throws, requiring size >= 1. Then `if (Helper.isNullOrEmpty(components.get(1)))` throws, requiring size >= 2. Thus, when the first subList call is made, `components.size()` is at least 2, so `fromIndex=1` < `toIndex >= 2` (or equal if size=2? Actually if size=2, fromIndex=1, toIndex=2, so fromIndex < toIndex, not >; also toIndex == size, not >). So all conditions are satisfied: fromIndex >= 0, toIndex <= size, fromIndex <= toIndex. For the second subList call, it occurs after accessing indices up to 7 (e.g., `components.get(5)`, `components.get(6)`, `components.get(7)`), which implies the list has at least 8 elements. So size >= 8, fromIndex=1, toIndex >= 8, again all conditions hold. Therefore, all throwing conditions of `IndexOutOfBoundsException` are avoided by the preceding validation and the fact that the list size is guaranteed to be sufficient.
answer: The only declared exception is `IndexOutOfBoundsException`. Its throwing conditions are fully avoided: `fromIndex < 0` is avoided because fromIndex is 1 (positive); `toIndex > size` is avoided because toIndex equals size; `fromIndex > toIndex` is avoided because size is at least 2 (and later at least 8) ensuring fromIndex <= toIndex. Thus, no exception is thrown by subList in this code.
